false_positives.evidence: The q query parameter is interpolated into a Sequelize SQL template literal.
false_positives.fix: Use parameterized replacements or Sequelize query-builder predicates for the search value.
false_positives.title: SQL injection in product search

trace.note: req.query.q is assigned to criteria.
criteria is interpolated into SQL passed to sequelize.query.

false_positives.why: A remote caller can alter the query and retrieve or modify database data beyond the intended product search.

false_positives.evidence: The authenticated caller's imageUrl is passed directly to fetch without destination validation.
false_positives.fix: Parse URLs and enforce an allowlist of public image hosts, with DNS/IP checks that reject private and link-local destinations.
false_positives.title: Profile image URL fetch permits SSRF

trace.note: url is read from req.body.imageUrl.
url is used as the fetch destination.

false_positives.why: Any authenticated user can make the server request internal services or cloud metadata endpoints.

false_positives.evidence: The password hashing helper uses crypto.createHash('md5') with no salt or work factor.
false_positives.fix: Migrate to Argon2id or bcrypt with unique salts and a calibrated work factor, rehashing at the next successful login.
false_positives.title: Passwords use unsalted MD5

trace.note: Cleartext passwords are passed to security.hash before storage.
MD5 produces the stored password hash.

false_positives.why: Stolen password hashes are inexpensive to crack offline and identical passwords produce identical hashes.

false_positives.evidence: A literal HMAC key is supplied directly to crypto.createHmac.
false_positives.fix: Move the key to a managed runtime secret, rotate it, and version stored HMACs for a controlled migration.
false_positives.title: HMAC secret is hard-coded in source
false_positives.why: Source disclosure exposes the key used to protect security-answer values, enabling offline guessing and forged values where that key is relied on.

false_positives.evidence: The id route parameter is interpolated into a $where JavaScript expression.
false_positives.fix: Use a structured equality selector such as find({ orderId: id }) and validate the expected order-ID format.
false_positives.title: Order lookup builds a MongoDB $where expression

trace.note: id derives from req.params.id.
id is interpolated into the $where selector.

false_positives.why: An unauthenticated caller can alter the selector and expose other orders or execute expensive database-side expressions.

false_positives.evidence: An archive entry path is concatenated into the write path and the containment condition only checks whether the resolved path contains the current directory.
false_positives.fix: Resolve each entry against a fixed extraction root and reject it unless the resolved path starts with that root plus a separator.
false_positives.title: ZIP extraction permits writes outside the upload directory

trace.note: fileName is taken from an archive entry.
The entry stream is written to a path built from fileName.

false_positives.why: A crafted archive can use traversal segments to overwrite files outside uploads/complaints when ZIP extraction is enabled.

false_positives.evidence: The profile update uses the token cookie but performs no CSRF token or exact Origin/Referer validation.
false_positives.fix: Use SameSite cookies and enforce an anti-CSRF token or strict exact Origin validation on cookie-authenticated state changes.
false_positives.title: Cookie-authenticated profile updates lack CSRF defenses

trace.note: Authentication tokens are stored in a cookie without a SameSite setting.
The request body changes the authenticated user's username.

false_positives.why: A malicious site can submit a cross-site request that changes a signed-in user's profile while the browser sends its cookie.

false_positives.evidence: The public /file-upload endpoint accepts an in-memory file before checks that only inspect filename extensions and do not impose a size limit.
false_positives.fix: Require authentication where appropriate, enforce Multer file-size limits, validate content by signature, and store uploads outside executable or application-readable paths.
false_positives.title: ZIP upload endpoint exposes an unrestricted file-write primitive

trace.note: A public multipart request supplies file.
The supplied buffer is handed to ZIP extraction.

false_positives.why: Untrusted uploads reach archive processing without authentication, content validation, or an effective size control; combined with archive extraction this permits hostile upload content.

false_positives.evidence: The checkout handler looks up BasketModel solely by req.params.id and later clears that basket's items without a UserId predicate.
false_positives.fix: Query and mutate the basket only with both its id and the authenticated user's id, preferably in a transaction.
false_positives.title: Basket checkout does not verify the basket owner

trace.note: The basket id comes from the route parameter.
The requested basket is loaded using only its id.
Items for that basket id are destroyed.

false_positives.why: A logged-in user can check out another customer's basket and alter its contents.

false_positives.evidence: hmac constructs a SHA-256 HMAC with a directly assigned secret literal.
false_positives.fix: Inject a rotated HMAC key from a secret manager or protected runtime configuration and remove the literal from source history.
false_positives.title: HMAC key is hard-coded in application source
false_positives.why: Source readers can reproduce security-answer HMACs and the secret cannot be rotated independently of a code release.

false_positives.evidence: The Node project declares version ranges in package.json but contains no package lockfile or npm shrinkwrap file.
false_positives.fix: Commit a package-lock.json generated from reviewed dependencies and enforce deterministic installs in CI.
false_positives.title: Node dependencies are not locked
false_positives.why: Builds can resolve different dependency versions over time, weakening reviewability and allowing known-vulnerable transitive versions to enter deployments unnoticed.

false_positives.evidence: POST /rest/user/login is registered without rate-limit middleware; the only nearby rate limit is for reset-password.
